name: Dana, Platform Lead at an AI coding-assistant startup
company_archetype: Series B developer-tools company with an IDE/CLI coding agent, ~40k weekly active developers
use_case: Agentic code editing: each turn re-sends a long, mostly identical context (system prompt, tool definitions, repo map, prior tool calls) and generates a short diff or tool call.

real_world_examples.summary: Pragmatic Engineer interview coverage: 'billions of code completions, daily', 100x growth in users and load in 12 months, Tab suggestions ideally under a second, inference on cloud GPUs. It does not discuss prefix caching in the visible text.

Secondary summary of Manus' engineering post: KV-cache hit rate is 'the single most important metric for a production agent'; typical task has ~100:1 input-to-output token ratio over ~50 tool calls. Primary post not re-fetched.
Retains KV cache in a radix tree so multi-turn chat and shared system prompts reuse prefix computation; up to 5x throughput claimed vs. baselines on the authors' benchmarks.

traffic_shape.peak_pattern: Weekday business hours (roughly 4x nights/weekends); no sharp spikes

why_pool: Input-heavy (~100:1) agent loops with long shared prefixes are where prefix-cache-aware packing helps most; steady daytime baseline justifies reserved GPUs; large coding model that is not in the serverless catalog.
why_burst: Not applicable: the 230B-class model is pool-only and never overflows. Daytime growth is handled by pre-scaling the pool on the weekday schedule, not by burst.
not_a_fit_if: Product promises sub-second time-to-first-token for inline completions (TTFT can rise under packing), or needs a frontier closed model, or needs P99 TPOT guarantees (PackServe targets median).

name: Marcus, Head of CX Engineering at a mid-size online retailer
company_archetype: Omnichannel retailer, ~$1.5B GMV, support chatbot deflecting order-status and returns questions
use_case: Customer-support chat assistant with a long shared system prompt (policies, tone, tool schema) plus per-customer order context; seasonal peak at Black Friday / Cyber Monday.

real_world_examples.summary: First month of its OpenAI-powered assistant: 2.3 million conversations, two-thirds of customer-service chats, <2 min resolution vs 11 min, work equal to 700 full-time agents (company-reported).
Cyber Monday 2025: $14.25B US online spend (+7.1% YoY); $16M/min at 8-10 pm peak; AI-driven traffic to US retail sites +670% on the day.

traffic_shape.peak_pattern: Black Friday weekend to Cyber Monday, evening-heavy; ~6x baseline for ~30 peak-hours/season; date known a year ahead

why_pool: Always-on support traffic with a large shared system prompt gives a steady, cache-friendly baseline; cost per GPU-hour is predictable and conversation data stays on infrastructure the retailer controls.
why_burst: 6x peak for a few days a year: reserving for peak wastes ~80% of GPU-hours; the model is in the serverless catalog so overflow gives identical answers while the pool scales up.
not_a_fit_if: Peak is sustained for weeks (just reserve it), serverless rate limits turn out to be below the overflow volume, or chat must meet a P99 latency SLA.

name: Priya, Director of Legal Engineering at a mid-market law firm / legal-tech vendor
company_archetype: Legal-tech team running contract review and data extraction for M&A diligence
use_case: Extract clauses and structured fields from long contracts and email sets; long document plus a fixed extraction schema/instructions prefix, JSON output.

real_world_examples.org: Thomson Reuters CoCounsel (Century Communities case study)
real_world_examples.summary: Homebuilder legal team uses it for reviewing contracts, summarizing documents, extracting data from large volumes of files; 87 land contracts reviewed in one M&A deal; avoided reading 10,000 emails. Vendor-reported, anecdotal.

traffic_shape.peak_pattern: Deal-closing crunches and month-end; batch queues tolerant of seconds of delay

why_pool: Confidential client documents argue for dedicated GPUs under the firm's control; extraction quality favors a large model; schema prefix is shared so cache-aware packing helps.
why_burst: Not applicable: large model is pool-only. Batch clients should honor 429 + Retry-After and queue; overflow to a smaller model would change answers and is deliberately not offered.
not_a_fit_if: Needs a model above the pool's ~230B class, or needs instant interactive latency during peaks without queuing, or requires contractual confidentiality terms Akamai has not published (unverified).

name: Dr. Amara, CMIO at a regional health system
company_archetype: Regional health system, ~3,000 clinicians, building an in-house ambient note-drafting service
use_case: Turn a visit transcript (~20 min) into a draft SOAP note using a fixed template prompt; clinician reviews before signing.

real_world_examples.summary: Homepage states 300+ health systems and 53M+ conversations powered each year; e.g. UW Health 800+ providers, 30 min/day documentation time saved; Inova 9,400+ clinicians.

traffic_shape.peak_pattern: Clinic hours on weekdays, bump at late morning and end of day; very quiet overnight

why_pool: Predictable diurnal clinic load fits a reserved pool; PHI data-control preference; note generation is not latency-critical per token so 50 ms is plenty.
why_burst: Burst is eligible by model but disabled by choice: sending PHI to a shared serverless pool needs compliance terms we cannot verify. Diurnal peaks are covered by scheduled scale-up.
not_a_fit_if: Compliance (e.g. HIPAA BAA) terms for Akamai GPU Linodes are not in place (unverified here), or clinicians need live in-visit suggestions with strict real-time latency.

name: Jo, Technical Director at a mid-size game studio
company_archetype: Studio shipping a live-service game with LLM-driven NPC dialogue
use_case: Short, in-character NPC replies generated per player utterance; each NPC has a fixed persona/world-state prefix.

real_world_examples.summary: R&D prototype with Nvidia Audio2Face and Inworld's LLM, human-written backstories, guardrails; Ubisoft says it is only a prototype and gives no latency or scale numbers.

traffic_shape.peak_pattern: Launch weekend and content drops, ~15x baseline for ~12 peak-hours per drop; dates known weeks ahead (assumed)

why_pool: Steady live-ops traffic with persona prefixes reused across a player's turns; 30 ms tier keeps short lines feeling instant.
why_burst: 15x launch spikes make peak reservation wasteful; gemma is in the serverless catalog, so overflow covers surprise load beyond the pre-scaled pool.
not_a_fit_if: Experience needs voice-to-voice round trips under ~1 s end to end, or serverless cannot hold a 30 ms TPOT (unpublished) and the studio cannot tolerate slower overflow.

name: Sam, Head of Product at a streaming/media company
company_archetype: Sports and news streamer generating personalized summaries and highlight scripts after live events
use_case: After each live event, generate personalized text recaps per viewer from event metadata and clip descriptions plus a viewer profile.

real_world_examples.summary: Paris 2024 personalized recaps: nearly 7 million variants possible, built from hundreds of NBC Sports clips a day, ~10 min playlists, 5,000 hours of coverage; NBCU editors reviewed content. (Peacock's underlying stack is not described in this source.)

traffic_shape.peak_pattern: Spike for ~2 h after each major event (about 8 per month); 40x baseline; schedule is public

why_pool: Small steady baseline (catalog, evergreen content) on reserved GPUs with shared event-context prefix across viewers.
why_burst: 40x peak lasting two hours is the textbook overflow case; hourly GPU billing makes short pre-scales costly and slow, and identical-model overflow keeps recap quality consistent.
not_a_fit_if: Recaps must arrive within seconds of the final whistle at full volume and serverless rate limits (unpublished) cannot absorb 80 rps; or recap quality requires a model not in the serverless catalog.

name: Kai, CTO at a voice-AI contact-center startup (POOR FIT)
company_archetype: Seed-stage voice agent vendor with contractual latency SLAs
use_case: Spoken conversations where every turn must start speaking within a hard latency budget; SLA written on P99.

real_world_examples.summary: Under a 50 ms median TPOT target, request-level P90 TPOT was about 80 ms (~1.6x), and production mean TTFT rose 66.4%; the paper says it is not a latency guarantee. No customer is claimed.

why_pool: Short prompts with a shared prefix would pack, but packing deliberately fills replicas close to the target, which hurts tails and TTFT.
why_burst: Serverless cold starts and unpublished rate limits make overflow unpredictable for a P99 SLA; burst is off.
not_a_fit_if: ALWAYS: the SLA is on P99 or time-to-first-token. This service targets median TPOT only. Use over-provisioned dedicated replicas without packing, or another vendor.

name: Lee, solo founder of a homework-help app (POOR FIT)
company_archetype: Two-person startup, student Q&A app with exam-season spikes
use_case: Students ask homework questions; short explanations generated. Usage is tiny most of the year and surges at finals.

real_world_examples.summary: Shows AI tutoring tools being timed to the school year; the source gives no usage numbers. The exam-season spike here is our extrapolation, not a cited fact.

traffic_shape.peak_pattern: Finals weeks (~20 peak-hours/month in season); near zero otherwise

why_pool: Weak: one replica is $4,320/month for 0.2 rps; no prefix sharing to exploit.
why_burst: The workload is better served entirely by serverless per-token billing; the pool adds cost with no benefit.
not_a_fit_if: Average utilization of even one replica is below roughly 20-30%. Use Akamai Inference serverless directly until sustained volume appears.
